title: Wire strippers, 10–18 AWG solid / 12–20 AWG stranded

sources.citation: game-design: unverified product-class pattern, for electrical-realism-reviewer to check against makers' catalogues. US electricians' wire strippers are commonly marked 10-18 AWG solid on one side of the jaws and 12-20 AWG stranded on the other: each physical hole carries a solid size and the stranded size one step smaller, because a stranded conductor is wider than a solid one of the same AWG. Modelled as one hole per marking (ten ids, stable save format), so a conductor stripped in a hole marked for another size or stranding nicks (plan D8).

game-design: unverified product-class features. Strippers of this class have cutting edges between the pivot and the holes (a cut capability up to 10 AWG, the largest hole), and some models add a slot that splits the outer jacket of 14/2 and 12/2 non-metallic sheathed cable (stripJacket up to 12 AWG conductors). The strip capability reaches the largest marked hole, 10 AWG.
